subject.title: fix(agents): make model-facing tool schemas llama.cpp GBNF-compatible (#108580)

question: Should OpenClaw fix this regression by removing business-rule length caps from the canonical model-facing schemas, as this PR does, or by adding a llama.cpp-specific provider projection?
rationale: Both approaches can restore llama.cpp inference, but they create different long-term compatibility contracts: canonical removal shifts all providers to downstream validation, while provider projection adds routing/configuration surface and may miss custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

options.title: Land canonical schema cleanup
options.body: Refresh and land this PR because the caps remain enforced by their runtime owners and custom llama.cpp endpoints cannot be reliably auto-detected.

options.title: Require provider projection
options.body: Pause this PR and adopt the competing profile-based approach only after it is cleanly rebased, documented for custom endpoints, and proven on its exact head.

recommendation.title: Land canonical schema cleanup
recommendation.body: Refresh and land this PR because the caps remain enforced by their runtime owners and custom llama.cpp endpoints cannot be reliably auto-detected.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history covers both the affected cron schema and the provider-cleaning boundary needed to choose between these implementations.
